solutions.check: 30 entries; each light the paper's grid did not give solved here from its clue's wordplay (an anagram or hidden word, the one listed word fitting every crossing) and its definition (WordNet), as the answer another puzzle gave the same clue, or as the one past answer its crossings left that the printed letters allow, agrees with the 29 answers the paper printed; printed-crossing fills: 2-down

clue.text: Thin animal — a sheep in wolf's clothing?

definitions.meaning: read literally, a big cat made of something as flimsy as stationery
a twist on the proverb: something meek dressed up to look fierce, a threat that is all show

explanation.surface: A scrawny beast turns out to be a harmless creature disguised as a predator.
explanation.walkthrough: The proverb is a wolf in sheep's clothing; reversing it describes something that looks menacing but is harmless.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom names a person or power that looks threatening but is actually weak, and the literal phrase is a flimsy cut-out cat.

clue.text: A model question

definitions.meaning: someone who strikes attitudes for an artist or photographer

explanation.definitionFit: It names both one who sits for an artist and a baffling problem or puzzle.

clue.text: Official policy formulated by person with glib talk

parts.note: party is a facetious or legal word for a person
a line is smooth persuasive patter, as in shooting a line

explanation.surface: A government policy devised by a smooth-talking individual.
explanation.definitionFit: The party line is the stance a political organisation officially takes and expects members to follow.

clue.text: Chicken order is held and processed

indicators.note: processed means worked over, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An order for a chicken is put on hold and dealt with.
explanation.walkthrough: 'processed' reworks ORDER IS HELD AND.
explanation.definitionFit: This is an American breed of domestic fowl with reddish-brown plumage.

clue.text: Fires began-soldier stood up

indicators.note: in a down clue stood up means the letters are read upwards, backwards

parts.note: set in means began, as winter set in
GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: Fires started, and a soldier got to his feet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stood up' turns SET IN plus GI upside down in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: To ignite something is to set it alight, just as firing it does.

clue.text: Ruler overthrown by agent infiltrating the capital

indicators.note: overthrown means turned over, so the whole run is read backwards
infiltrating puts one piece inside another

parts.note: Rome is the capital city, the seat of ancient empire
a rep is a sales representative or agent

explanation.surface: A leader is toppled by a spy who has slipped into the capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'infiltrating' gives ROREPME, which 'overthrown' turns end to end; 'the capital' needs no country named because Rome is the capital of empire.
explanation.definitionFit: An emperor is the sovereign of an empire, the supreme ruler.

clue.text: War spoils the planet

definitions.meaning: the Roman god of war, whose name stands for war itself
damages or disfigures, as a verb
the red fourth planet from the Sun

explanation.surface: Conflict ruins the Earth.
explanation.walkthrough: A triple definition: the god of war, a verb meaning damages, and the red planet all share one spelling.
explanation.definitionFit: The Roman war god, the verb meaning blemishes, and the fourth planet all carry this single name.

clue.text: Maiden's taken off bad dress

indicators.note: taken off means removed from the word for bad

parts.note: malign means evil or harmful
M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over; the 's is a link meaning has

explanation.surface: A girl has removed an ugly frock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dress' is military: to dress ranks is to line soldiers up straight.
explanation.definitionFit: To dress troops is to arrange them in straight lines, putting them in line.

clue.text: Cleaner in rush for extra money

indicators.note: in puts the cleaner's word within the word for rush

parts.note: a surge is a sudden rush
a char is a charwoman, a domestic cleaner

explanation.surface: A cleaning lady in a hurry wants more pay.
explanation.walkthrough: A char is a dated British word for a woman paid to clean houses.
explanation.definitionFit: A surcharge is an additional fee added to the normal price.

clue.text: Carry on practising, being keen — had pension adjusted

indicators.note: adjusted means altered, so the letters are reset in a new order

explanation.surface: An eager pensioner keeps up training after a pension change.
explanation.walkthrough: 'adjusted' reworks KEEN HAD PENSION.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means keeping up a skill by doing it occasionally so as not to lose it.

clue.text: King portrayed in oils, in cooking a roast

indicators.note: cooking suggests ingredients being worked over, so the letters are mixed up

parts.note: R is short for rex, Latin for king
taken as written

explanation.surface: A monarch painted in oils while a joint of meat is being roasted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooking' mixes R with OILS to give SIRLO; the second 'in' is then added as IN. 'portrayed' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Sirloin is a prime cut of beef usually served as a joint for roasting.

clue.text: Law perhaps curtailed first showing of film

indicators.note: curtailed means having its tail cut off, so the final letter goes

parts.note: a film's opening public screening is its premiere

explanation.surface: A legal rule, cut short, at a film's gala opening night.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Law' is not legislation but Andrew Bonar Law, British Prime Minister in 1922-23; 'perhaps' marks him as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Bonar Law served as Britain's prime minister, so he is an example of a head of government.

clue.text: A name for McGonagall? Try Hermes, possibly

indicators.note: possibly signals that the letters could be arranged another way

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Suggesting the messenger god as a name for a poet.
explanation.walkthrough: William McGonagall was a Scottish versifier famous as the worst poet in English, so a dismissive word for a verse-maker fits him.
explanation.definitionFit: A rhymester is a writer of trivial or poor verse, which is how McGonagall is remembered.

clue.text: Drink wallop

definitions.meaning: a mixed bowl of fruit juice and spirits served at parties
a hard blow with the fist

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a fruity mixed party beverage and a hard blow with the fist.

clue.text: Felicity needs about one pound two shillings

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the words one and pound are read backwards

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
lb is the abbreviation for a pound weight
s is the abbreviation for a shilling in old British money, so two give SS

explanation.surface: Happiness requires roughly a pound and two shillings.
explanation.walkthrough: Felicity looks like a woman's name but means happiness. The shilling was a pre-1971 British coin, abbreviated s.
explanation.definitionFit: Felicity is a formal word for intense happiness, and bliss is perfect joy.

clue.text: Brachycephalic vegetable?

parts.note: brachycephalic means short and wide in the skull, so a vegetable with a wide head; really a common garden legume

explanation.surface: A medical term for a short-skulled vegetable.
explanation.walkthrough: Brachycephalic means having a broad head, and a bean has a 'head' only in a jokey sense.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a large flat legume, read jokingly as a pulse with a wide skull.

clue.text: The way river attracts fisherman, he's a killer

parts.note: St is short for street, a way or road
R is the map abbreviation for river
an angler fishes with rod and line

explanation.surface: A road by a river draws an angler, who turns out to be a murderer.
explanation.definitionFit: A strangler kills by throttling, so this is a kind of murderer.

clue.text: Put some oil in blue car — it's broken down

indicators.note: broken down suggests a wrecked machine, so the letters are reassembled

parts.note: the word it, with the 's a link meaning is

explanation.surface: A blue car that has broken down needs some oil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broken down' rearranges BLUE CAR IT.
explanation.definitionFit: To lubricate a machine is to apply grease to its moving parts.

clue.text: Begin shortly to share out the work

indicators.note: shortly means cut short, so the word for begin loses its last letter

parts.note: to begin something is to open it
to ration is to share out in fixed amounts

explanation.surface: Instructions to start soon and divide up the jobs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shortly' looks like 'soon' but trims OPEN to OPE.
explanation.definitionFit: An operation is a piece of work or activity, as in a military or business undertaking.

clue.text: Popular student, we hear, has some bite

indicators.note: we hear means the clue words are spoken and their sound gives the spelling

parts.note: in means popular, and a sizar is a Cambridge or Dublin undergraduate on a grant

explanation.surface: A well-liked undergraduate turns out to be sharp-tongued.
explanation.walkthrough: A sizar is a student at Cambridge or Trinity College Dublin who receives financial help; IN SIZAR spoken matches the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An incisor is a front cutting tooth, the one that gives a creature its bite.

clue.text: Famous for turkeys and not people

parts.note: nor means and not
folk means people

explanation.surface: A place celebrated for its turkeys rather than its inhabitants.
explanation.walkthrough: NORFOLK is an English county known for its turkey farming.
explanation.definitionFit: This East Anglian county gives its name to a well-known breed of turkey.

clue.text: Island's turned black

indicators.note: turned means the word is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: Elba is the Mediterranean island of Napoleon's exile; the possessive supplies the S

explanation.surface: An island has gone dark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned' reverses ELBAS.
explanation.definitionFit: Sable is the heraldic and poetic term for the colour black.

clue.text: Daughter keen to be a harpist

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for daughter in family trees
avid means eager or keen

explanation.surface: A girl is eager to become a harp player.
explanation.walkthrough: The Biblical King David played the harp to soothe Saul.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Bible the young shepherd who became king soothed Saul by playing the harp.

clue.text: Asp given by somebody to queen of old

parts.note: a VIP, very important person, is a somebody
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, a queen of the past

explanation.surface: A snake handed to an ancient queen by someone.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface recalls Cleopatra, the queen of old killed by an asp.
explanation.definitionFit: The asp is a species of venomous snake of the adder family.

clue.text: Grant I had, amongst women soldiers once, some female supporters

parts.note: Cary Grant was the Hollywood film star

indicators.note: amongst places one piece within the letters of another

parts.note: the ATS was the Auxiliary Territorial Service, the British women's army of World War II
I'd is the contraction of I had

explanation.surface: A man named Grant among women in uniform, with some ladies backing him.
explanation.walkthrough: The ATS is the old British women's army corps. 'Supporters' are architectural, not fans.
explanation.definitionFit: Caryatids are stone columns carved as draped women that hold up a building's roof.

clue.text: Was partisan part of this? I deduce so

indicators.note: part of signals the answer is a stretch within the words that follow

explanation.surface: A detective concludes that someone was biased.
explanation.definitionFit: To have sided with one camp is to have taken a partisan stance.

clue.text: Talk fast

definitions.meaning: to put into words, voice an opinion
rapid, like a non-stopping train or speedy delivery

explanation.definitionFit: To voice something is to put it into words, and a rapid train or delivery is also called this.

clue.text: A game one's left on the shelf

definitions.meaning: a children's card game in which players avoid being left holding one card
an unmarried woman past the usual age of marrying, in old-fashioned slang

explanation.definitionFit: It names a card game about avoiding the odd card, and a dated term for a woman who never married.

clue.text: Ultimately the numbers 7 + 5 + 4 + 2 make 5

indicators.note: ultimately means at the end, so the final letter of each number word is taken

parts.note: the number written as a word
the number written as a word
the number written as a word
the number written as a word

explanation.surface: An arithmetic sum adding up to five.
explanation.walkthrough: Spell out seven, five, four and two and take their last letters. The final '5' points to 5 Down, EMPEROR.
explanation.definitionFit: Nero was the Roman emperor of the first century, so he answers the cross-reference to the ruler at 5 Down.

clue.text: No tower of strength, this destitute royal in want

parts.note: broke means without money

indicators.note: in places the royal letter inside the word for want

parts.note: need is want or lack
R stands for rex or regina, king or queen

explanation.surface: A penniless member of the royal family in need is no pillar of support.
explanation.definitionFit: A broken reed is an idiom for a person who proves unreliable just when support is needed.
